raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Enable symmetric compressed-tensors W4A16 linear layers on ROCm using optional vLLM GPTQ operators, with format/shape guards and FP16 arithmetic. Supports the vLLM operator signatures from before and after vllm-project/vllm#54809.

Ported from patch 7 in my [strix-halo-sglang](https://github.com/JeremiahM37/strix-halo-sglang) repo.

Validation on gfx1151: 26 tests passed, with real numerical cases on standalone builds of both vLLM GPTQ kernel versions; pre-commit passed. `jy395/Qwen3-8B-rtn-w4a16` with every quantized Linear served through this scheme scored 85/100 on gsm8k, against 88/100 for a dense model from the same checkpoint. Full-server integration and a real vLLM install have not been tested.

nodes.body:
A partial check on RDNA4 (gfx1201), on current `main` + #43679 + #47254, in a stock `rocm/pytorch` image:

- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_wna16_rocm.py`: **8 passed, 2 skipped, 20 subtests passed** with this PR. On the base the file can't run (pytest rc=4).
- I couldn't validate end to end, for two reasons:
  - The image has no vLLM, so the optional vLLM GPTQ operators this path uses aren't available there.
  - The common `RedHatAI/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` checkpoint is rejected earlier by the installed `compressed-tensors` library (`actorder='group' has been removed`), with or without this PR.

If you have a symmetric checkpoint that loads with current `compressed-tensors`, I'm happy to run it on RDNA3/RDNA4 with gsm8k and throughput.

Thanks @vivienfanghuagood. Try `jy395/Qwen3-8B-rtn-w4a16`: symmetric 4-bit, group size 128, `pack-quantized`, no `actorder`. Its config validates under compressed-tensors 0.16.0, 0.18.0 and 0.20.1. `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-W4A16-e2e` is the same format if you want a quick load first.

I've rebased onto current `main` and added a commit for vllm-project/vllm#54809, which removed `g_idx` from `gptq_gemm` and `gptq_shuffle`. Both signatures now work, so please test the new head.

What I ran with that checkpoint on gfx1151, with every quantized Linear served through this scheme, against a dense model built from the same checkpoint:

| | This PR | Dense FP16 |
|---|---:|---:|
| gsm8k, first 100, greedy | 85/100 | 88/100 |
| Throughput, batch 8 | 51.6 tok/s | 26.4 tok/s |
| Relative error per layer, against exact | 0.09–0.15% | 0.02% |

- The kernel shows no scale bias (1.00000 on the layers I checked), so I read the extra error as its FP16 accumulation. The gsm8k gap is 3 questions on a sample of 100, so it doesn't separate the two.
- This isn't a server run. It used a Hugging Face model with standalone builds of vLLM's GPTQ kernels, not a vLLM install, and I stubbed `sgl_kernel` at import because this path doesn't call it. I also haven't run it on RDNA3 or RDNA4, so your gsm8k and throughput run would cover what's missing.
- `actorder: weight` or `static` checkpoints, which is most current GPTQ uploads, are still refused here. compressed-tensors documents that these don't change the stored format, so they could be allowed, but I haven't tested that. I can add it if you think it belongs in this PR.

<!-- pr-check-comment runs=41753740786 -->
Required checks failed on e90f32d; this PR cannot be merged until they pass.

Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend. Reverts must use GitHub's default format: Revert "original title". Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
Edit the title; the check reruns on its own.

RDNA4 (gfx1201) results at your head `e90f32d86d`, applied on `main` 57bfde9f2c. Setup:
- `rocm/vllm` ROCm 10.0 image: vLLM 0.27.1, which has the pre-vllm-project/vllm#54809 GPTQ signatures, and torch 2.12.
- `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, Triton attention, one GPU.

**What works**
- `test_compressed_tensors_wna16_rocm.py`: 26 passed, 76 subtests passed.
- `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-W4A16-e2e` loads and serves.
- Op level, this PR's conversion followed by `gptq_shuffle` / `gptq_gemm` (ExLlama), against an fp32 dequantized reference. Inputs were random symmetric int4 weights, group size 128, with shapes N x K = 4096 x 4096, 12288 x 4096 and 4096 x 12288, and M = 1, 8, 64 and 512. Relative error was at most 1.5e-3.
- In the served model, layer 0's packed weights and scales match the checkpoint exactly. That includes the merged qkv and gate_up.
- On raw-text requests, every W4A16 Linear in `jy395/Qwen3-8B-rtn-w4a16` matches x @ dequant(W)^T within 7e-3 relative error.

**What fails: chat-template prompts give NaN**
- With raw text the model is fine. "The capital of France is" continues with " Paris. The capital", the same as bf16 Qwen3-8B. Raw prompts from 5 to 446 tokens all gave sensible continuations.
- Any prompt in the chat template returns `!!!!...` (token 0). gsm8k (100 questions, chat template, as `sgl-eval` sends it) scores 0%.
- Where it starts: on a 20-token chat-template prompt, the input to block 6's `down_proj` reaches |x| = 9408. The fp32 reference output peaks at 18912, which fits in fp16, but `gptq_gemm` returns 2 non-finite values. From block 7 on, every layer's input is NaN.
- So the overflow appears to be inside the ExLlama kernel's fp16 arithmetic, not in the final values. It shows up with Qwen3's large activations, which appear on prompts with the chat special tokens.
- Did your gsm8k run use the chat template? The raw-text prompts I tried don't trigger it.

**Throughput**

Random 512 in / 256 out (token ids, so no chat tokens), same server settings:

| | c=1 tok/s (TPOT) | c=8 tok/s (TPOT) |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | 37.8 (26.2 ms) | 273.5 (28.0 ms) |
| this PR, `jy395/Qwen3-8B-rtn-w4a16` | 63.3 (14.9 ms) | 303.8 (21.3 ms) |

bf16 Qwen3-8B in the same environment scores 95% on the same gsm8k setup.

I'll post RDNA3 (gfx1100) results with vLLM 0.31, which has the new signatures, in a follow-up.

Follow-up with RDNA3 (gfx1100, W7900-class) results. Same PR head (`e90f32d86d`) on `main` 57bfde9f2c. This run uses vLLM 0.31.0, which has the post-vllm-project/vllm#54809 signatures, and torch 2.13 (ROCm 7.2). `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, Triton attention, one GPU.

**Same as on gfx1201**
- `test_compressed_tensors_wna16_rocm.py`: 26 passed, 76 subtests passed.
- `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-W4A16-e2e` loads and serves.
- `jy395/Qwen3-8B-rtn-w4a16` is fine on raw text: "The capital of France is" gives " Paris. The capital of the region of Île-de-F...".
- With the chat template it returns `!!!!...`, so I skipped gsm8k. bf16 `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` in the same environment answers the same chat prompt with "84" and scores 91% on gsm8k (100 questions).

**Op level**

Same check as before: random symmetric int4, group size 128, this PR's conversion followed by `gptq_shuffle` / `gptq_gemm` (ExLlama), against an fp32 reference. With vLLM 0.31 on gfx1100 the error grows at larger M:

| N x K | M = 1, 8 | M = 64, 512 |
|---|---|---|
| 4096 x 4096 | 9.5e-4 | 6.6e-3 |
| 12288 x 4096 | 9.4e-4 | 6.6e-3 |
| 4096 x 12288 | 1.5e-3 | 1.1e-2 |

The same shapes on gfx1201 with vLLM 0.27 gave 2.8e-4 at M = 64 and 512, so the large-M path differs between the two builds.

**Throughput**

Random 512 in / 256 out (token ids, so no chat tokens), same server settings:

| | c=1 tok/s (TPOT) | c=8 tok/s (TPOT) |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | 24.2 (40.9 ms) | 178.4 (42.9 ms) |
| this PR, `jy395/Qwen3-8B-rtn-w4a16` | 70.5 (13.6 ms) | 376.9 (19.4 ms) |

So on both RDNA3 and RDNA4 the speedup is there. The blocker for Qwen3 is the chat-template NaN described in my previous comment.

files.patch:
@@ -9,3 +9,19 @@ set. `mxfp4-pack-quantized` linears are not supported yet: the dense FP4 Marlin
 kernel is only instantiated for group_size 16 and cannot decode E8M0 scales. If
 you have requirements for other formats, you can submit an issue through this
 [link](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues).
+
+## ROCm W4A16 linear layers
+
+Symmetric 4-bit group/channel checkpoints can use the optional ROCm vLLM GPTQ
+operators (`gptq_gemm` with `use_v2_format`, and `gptq_shuffle`, as in vLLM
+0.16). Both that signature and the one after
+[vllm-project/vllm#54809](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54809),
+which dropped the `g_idx` argument, are supported: the installed signature is
+detected once per weight load and adapted to transparently. Supported group
+sizes are 32, 64, 128, or channelwise; activation ordering is unsupported (and
+with a post-#54809 vLLM, whose kernels dropped activation-order support
+entirely, cannot be requested at all), and each local weight partition must
+have K and N divisible by 128.
+The kernel uses FP16 arithmetic. BF16 activations and scales are converted to
+FP16, so models must stay within FP16's numerical range. Checkpoint scales that
+overflow FP16 are rejected during loading. CUDA continues to use Marlin.

@@ -2,6 +2,7 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import inspect
 import logging
 from typing import Callable, Optional
 
@@ -39,9 +40,10 @@
     replace_parameter,
     unpack_cols,
 )
-from sglang.srt.utils import is_cuda
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_cuda, is_hip
 
 _is_cuda = is_cuda()
+_is_hip = is_hip()
 
 if _is_cuda:
     from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.gptq_marlin_repack import gptq_marlin_repack
@@ -51,6 +53,115 @@
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
+
+_OLD_SHUFFLE_NPARAMS = 3  # gptq_shuffle(q_weight, g_idx, bit)
+_NEW_SHUFFLE_NPARAMS = 2  # gptq_shuffle(q_weight, bit)
+_OLD_GEMM_NPARAMS = 8  # gptq_gemm(a, b_q_weight, b_gptq_qzeros, b_gptq_scales, g_idx, use_exllama, use_v2_format, bit)
+_NEW_GEMM_NPARAMS = 7  # gptq_gemm(a, b_q_weight, b_gptq_qzeros, b_gptq_scales, use_exllama, use_v2_format, bit)
+
+
+def _signature_kind(fn: Callable, name: str, old_nparams: int, new_nparams: int) -> str:
+    """Classify a vLLM ROCm GPTQ op as "old" or "new", rejecting anything
+    else with a clear error.
+
+    Only vLLM's real Python wrappers (``vllm._custom_ops.gptq_shuffle`` /
+    ``gptq_gemm``) are supported: plain ``def``s with a fixed, introspectable
+    argument count. A raw/opaque callable -- e.g. an un-wrapped
+    ``torch.ops._C`` op, whose Python-visible signature is ``(*args,
+    **kwargs)`` -- is deliberately never classified as either API: it is
+    rejected instead of silently guessed at.
+    """
+    try:
+        params = inspect.signature(fn).parameters
+    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
+        raise NotImplementedError(
+            f"ROCm WNA16 could not read {name}'s signature ({fn!r}): {exc}. "
+            "Only vLLM's plain Python vllm._custom_ops wrapper is supported, "
+            "not an opaque or raw-bound callable."
+        ) from exc
+    if any(
+        p.kind in (inspect.Parameter.VAR_POSITIONAL, inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD)
+        for p in params.values()
+    ):
+        raise NotImplementedError(
+            f"ROCm WNA16 does not support an opaque {name} signature "
+            f"{inspect.signature(fn)}; pass vLLM's plain Python "
+            f"vllm._custom_ops.{name} wrapper, not a raw/variadic callable."
+        )
+    nparams = len(params)
+    if nparams == old_nparams:
+        return "old"
+    if nparams == new_nparams:
+        return "new"
+    raise NotImplementedError(
+        f"ROCm WNA16 does not recognize {name}'s signature "
+        f"{inspect.signature(fn)} ({nparams} params); expected {old_nparams} "
+        f"(pre-vllm-project/vllm#54809) or {new_nparams} (post-#54809)."
+    )
+
+
+def _bind_rocm_gptq_ops(gptq_shuffle: Callable, gptq_gemm: Callable) -> tuple:
+    """Adapt to either GPTQ ROCm op signature vLLM may expose.
+
+    vllm-project/vllm#54809 ("[Quant][Kernel] Remove GPTQ Group/Dynamic
+    Activation Ordering", 2026-09-08) dropped the g_idx argument from
+    ``gptq_shuffle``/``gptq_gemm``: the ROCm kernels themselves no longer
+    accept an activation-order permutation (the CUDA-graph-friendly
+    identity-order path becomes the only path). This module never builds a
+    non-trivial g_idx -- activation ordering is already rejected in
+    __init__ -- so we bind wrappers that keep the old (pre-#54809, e.g.
+    rocm/sgl-dev:rocm7-vllm-20250904) call shape our callers use, dropping
+    the always-empty g_idx when the installed vLLM no longer accepts it.
+    """
+    shuffle_kind = _signature_kind(
+        gptq_shuffle, "gptq_shuffle", _OLD_SHUFFLE_NPARAMS, _NEW_SHUFFLE_NPARAMS
+    )
+    gemm_kind = _signature_kind(
+        gptq_gemm, "gptq_gemm", _OLD_GEMM_NPARAMS, _NEW_GEMM_NPARAMS
+    )
+    if shuffle_kind != gemm_kind:
+        raise NotImplementedError(
+            f"ROCm WNA16 found mismatched vLLM GPTQ op signatures: "
+            f"gptq_shuffle looks {shuffle_kind} ({inspect.signature(gptq_shuffle)}) "
+            f"but gptq_gemm looks {gemm_kind} ({inspect.signature(gptq_gemm)}). "
+            "Check the installed vLLM build."
+        )
+    if shuffle_kind == "old":
+        return gptq_shuffle, gptq_gemm
+
+    def shuffle(q_weight: torch.Tensor, g_idx: torch.Tensor, bit: int) -> None:
+        if g_idx.numel():
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "ROCm WNA16 activation ordering is unsupported: the installed "
+                "vLLM's gptq_shuffle no longer accepts g_idx "
+                "(vllm-project/vllm#54809)."
+            )
+        gptq_shuffle(q_weight, bit)
+
+    def gemm(
+        a: torch.Tensor,
+        b_q_weight: torch.Tensor,
+        b_gptq_qzeros: torch.Tensor,
+        b_gptq_scales: torch.Tensor,
+        g_idx: torch.Tensor,
+        use_exllama: bool,
+        use_v2_format: bool,
+        bit: int,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if g_idx.numel():
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "ROCm WNA16 activation ordering is unsupported: the installed "
+                "vLLM's gptq_gemm no longer accepts g_idx "
+                "(vllm-project/vllm#54809)."
+            )
+        return gptq_gemm(
+            a, b_q_weight, b_gptq_qzeros, b_gptq_scales, use_exllama,
+            use_v2_format, bit,
+        )
+
+    return shuffle, gemm
+
+
 __all__ = ["CompressedTensorsWNA16", "XPUCompressedTensorsWNA16"]
 WNA16_SUPPORTED_TYPES_MAP = {
     4: scalar_types.uint4b8,
@@ -70,6 +181,18 @@ def __init__(self,
                  symmetric: Optional[bool] = True,
                  actorder: Optional[ActivationOrdering] = None):
 
+        if _is_hip and (
+            num_bits != 4
+            or not symmetric
+            or actorder is not None
+            or strategy not in ("group", "channel")
+            or group_size not in (None, -1, 32, 64, 128)
+        ):
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "ROCm WNA16 requires symmetric 4-bit group/channel quantization "
+                "without activation ordering (group_size: -1, 32, 64, 128)."
+            )
+
         self.pack_factor = 32 // num_bits
         self.strategy = strategy
         self.symmetric = symmetric
@@ -116,6 +239,14 @@ def create_weights(self, layer: torch.nn.Module, output_size: int,
             has_g_idx=self.has_g_idx
         )
 
+        if _is_hip:
+            if params_dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+                raise NotImplementedError("ROCm WNA16 requires float16 or bfloat16.")
+            if input_size_per_partition % 128 or output_size_per_partition % 128:
+                raise NotImplementedError(
+                    "ROCm WNA16 requires partition dimensions divisible by 128."
+                )
+
         # If group_size is -1, we are in channelwise case.
         group_size = self.group_size if self.group_size != -1 else input_size
         row_parallel = (input_size != input_size_per_partition)
@@ -205,9 +336,62 @@ def create_weights(self, layer: torch.nn.Module, output_size: int,
                                             weight_loader=weight_loader)
             layer.register_parameter("weight_g_idx", weight_g_idx)
 
+    def _process_weights_rocm(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        # These optional ops are supplied by ROCm vLLM builds. Do not import
+        # vLLM at module scope: CUDA and other quantization schemes do not need it.
+        try:
+            from vllm._custom_ops import gptq_gemm, gptq_shuffle
+        except ImportError as exc:
+            raise ImportError(
+                "ROCm compressed-tensors W4A16 requires a ROCm vLLM build "
+                "providing gptq_gemm and gptq_shuffle."
+            ) from exc
+
+        rocm_gptq_shuffle, self._rocm_gptq_gemm = _bind_rocm_gptq_ops(
+            gptq_shuffle, gptq_gemm
+        )
+        k, n = self.kernel_config.partition_weight_shape
+        group_size = k if self.group_size == -1 else self.group_size
+        if k % group_size:
+            raise ValueError("ROCm WNA16 input partition must contain whole groups.")
+
+        # The checkpoint packs unsigned (signed + 8) nibbles along K, in
+        # [N, K/8] order. GPTQ wants [K/8, N]; scales follow the same transpose.
+        # Use the checkpoint layout, not a shape heuristic (square shapes
+        # cannot distinguish the two orientations).
+        if tuple(layer.weight_packed.shape) != (n, k // 8):
+            raise ValueError("Unexpected compressed-tensors packed weight shape.")
+        if tuple(layer.weight_scale.shape) != (n, k // group_size):
+            raise ValueError("Unexpected compressed-tensors scale shape.")
+        qweight = layer.weight_packed.t().contiguous()
+        scales = layer.weight_scale.t().contiguous().to(torch.float16)
+        if not torch.isfinite(scales).all():
+            raise ValueError("ROCm WNA16 scales must be finite in float16.")
+
+        # GPTQ v1 stores zero - 1: symmetric CT's zero=8 becomes eight 7s
+        # per int32. No unpack/repack or full dequantization is necessary.
+        qzeros = torch.full(
+            (k // group_size, n // 8),
+            0x77777777,
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device=qweight.device,
+        )
+        g_idx = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int32, device=qweight.device)
+        rocm_gptq_shuffle(qweight, g_idx, 4)
+
+        # Replace the checkpoint parameters rather than retaining duplicate
+        # packed weights/scales alongside the serving representation.
+        replace_parameter(layer, "weight_packed", qweight)
+        replace_parameter(layer, "weight_scale", scales)
+        layer.register_buffer("rocm_qzeros", qzeros)
+        layer.register_buffer("rocm_g_idx", g_idx)
+
     # Checkpoints are serialized in compressed-tensors format, which is
     # different from the format the kernel may want. Handle repacking here.
     def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        if _is_hip:
+            self._process_weights_rocm(layer)
+            return
         # Default names since marlin requires empty parameters for these,
         # TODO: remove this requirement from marlin (allow optional tensors)
         self.w_q_name = "weight_packed"
@@ -303,6 +487,31 @@ def transform_w_s(x):
 
     def apply_weights(self, layer: torch.nn.Module, x: torch.Tensor,
                       bias: Optional[torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if _is_hip:
+            if x.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+                raise TypeError("ROCm WNA16 requires float16 or bfloat16 input.")
+            if x.shape[-1] != self.kernel_config.partition_weight_shape[0]:
+                raise ValueError("ROCm WNA16 input does not match the weight partition.")
+            output_shape = (
+                *x.shape[:-1], self.kernel_config.partition_weight_shape[1]
+            )

+def make_layer(
+    k=256, n=128, group_size=128, dtype=torch.float16, full_k=None, full_n=None
+):
+    scheme = wna16.CompressedTensorsWNA16(
+        strategy="channel" if group_size == -1 else "group",
+        num_bits=4,
+        group_size=group_size,
+    )
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    scheme.create_weights(
+        layer,
+        output_size=full_n or n,
+        input_size=full_k or k,
+        output_partition_sizes=[n],
+        input_size_per_partition=k,
+        params_dtype=dtype,
+        weight_loader=lambda *args, **kwargs: None,
+    )
+    # Deterministic signed values exercise every nibble, including -8 and +7.
+    signed = (
+        (torch.arange(n * k).reshape(n, k) * 7 + torch.arange(n).unsqueeze(1)) % 16 - 8
+    ).to(torch.int8)
+    groups = 1 if group_size == -1 else k // group_size
+    scales = (torch.arange(n * groups).reshape(n, groups) % 17 + 1).to(dtype) / 128
+    layer.weight_packed.data.copy_(pack_to_int32(signed, 4))
+    layer.weight_scale.data.copy_(scales)
+    group_size = k if group_size == -1 else group_size
+    reference = signed.float() * scales.float().repeat_interleave(group_size, dim=1)

issue_comments.body:
A partial check on RDNA4 (gfx1201), on current `main` + #43679 + #47254, in a stock `rocm/pytorch` image:

- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_wna16_rocm.py`: **8 passed, 2 skipped, 20 subtests passed** with this PR. On the base the file can't run (pytest rc=4).
- I couldn't validate end to end, for two reasons:
  - The image has no vLLM, so the optional vLLM GPTQ operators this path uses aren't available there.
  - The common `RedHatAI/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` checkpoint is rejected earlier by the installed `compressed-tensors` library (`actorder='group' has been removed`), with or without this PR.

If you have a symmetric checkpoint that loads with current `compressed-tensors`, I'm happy to run it on RDNA3/RDNA4 with gsm8k and throughput.

Thanks @vivienfanghuagood. Try `jy395/Qwen3-8B-rtn-w4a16`: symmetric 4-bit, group size 128, `pack-quantized`, no `actorder`. Its config validates under compressed-tensors 0.16.0, 0.18.0 and 0.20.1. `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-W4A16-e2e` is the same format if you want a quick load first.

I've rebased onto current `main` and added a commit for vllm-project/vllm#54809, which removed `g_idx` from `gptq_gemm` and `gptq_shuffle`. Both signatures now work, so please test the new head.

What I ran with that checkpoint on gfx1151, with every quantized Linear served through this scheme, against a dense model built from the same checkpoint:

| | This PR | Dense FP16 |
|---|---:|---:|
| gsm8k, first 100, greedy | 85/100 | 88/100 |
| Throughput, batch 8 | 51.6 tok/s | 26.4 tok/s |
| Relative error per layer, against exact | 0.09–0.15% | 0.02% |

- The kernel shows no scale bias (1.00000 on the layers I checked), so I read the extra error as its FP16 accumulation. The gsm8k gap is 3 questions on a sample of 100, so it doesn't separate the two.
- This isn't a server run. It used a Hugging Face model with standalone builds of vLLM's GPTQ kernels, not a vLLM install, and I stubbed `sgl_kernel` at import because this path doesn't call it. I also haven't run it on RDNA3 or RDNA4, so your gsm8k and throughput run would cover what's missing.
- `actorder: weight` or `static` checkpoints, which is most current GPTQ uploads, are still refused here. compressed-tensors documents that these don't change the stored format, so they could be allowed, but I haven't tested that. I can add it if you think it belongs in this PR.

- `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-W4A16-e2e` loads and serves.
- Op level, this PR's conversion followed by `gptq_shuffle` / `gptq_gemm` (ExLlama), against an fp32 dequantized reference. Inputs were random symmetric int4 weights, group size 128, with shapes N x K = 4096 x 4096, 12288 x 4096 and 4096 x 12288, and M = 1, 8, 64 and 512. Relative error was at most 1.5e-3.
- In the served model, layer 0's packed weights and scales match the checkpoint exactly. That includes the merged qkv and gate_up.
- On raw-text requests, every W4A16 Linear in `jy395/Qwen3-8B-rtn-w4a16` matches x @ dequant(W)^T within 7e-3 relative error.

**What fails: chat-template prompts give NaN**
- With raw text the model is fine. "The capital of France is" continues with " Paris. The capital", the same as bf16 Qwen3-8B. Raw prompts from 5 to 446 tokens all gave sensible continuations.
- Any prompt in the chat template returns `!!!!...` (token 0). gsm8k (100 questions, chat template, as `sgl-eval` sends it) scores 0%.
- Where it starts: on a 20-token chat-template prompt, the input to block 6's `down_proj` reaches |x| = 9408. The fp32 reference output peaks at 18912, which fits in fp16, but `gptq_gemm` returns 2 non-finite values. From block 7 on, every layer's input is NaN.
- So the overflow appears to be inside the ExLlama kernel's fp16 arithmetic, not in the final values. It shows up with Qwen3's large activations, which appear on prompts with the chat special tokens.
- Did your gsm8k run use the chat template? The raw-text prompts I tried don't trigger it.

Follow-up with RDNA3 (gfx1100, W7900-class) results. Same PR head (`e90f32d86d`) on `main` 57bfde9f2c. This run uses vLLM 0.31.0, which has the post-vllm-project/vllm#54809 signatures, and torch 2.13 (ROCm 7.2). `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, Triton attention, one GPU.

**Same as on gfx1201**
- `test_compressed_tensors_wna16_rocm.py`: 26 passed, 76 subtests passed.
- `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-W4A16-e2e` loads and serves.
- `jy395/Qwen3-8B-rtn-w4a16` is fine on raw text: "The capital of France is" gives " Paris. The capital of the region of Île-de-F...".
- With the chat template it returns `!!!!...`, so I skipped gsm8k. bf16 `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` in the same environment answers the same chat prompt with "84" and scores 91% on gsm8k (100 questions).

**Op level**

Same check as before: random symmetric int4, group size 128, this PR's conversion followed by `gptq_shuffle` / `gptq_gemm` (ExLlama), against an fp32 reference. With vLLM 0.31 on gfx1100 the error grows at larger M:

| N x K | M = 1, 8 | M = 64, 512 |
|---|---|---|
| 4096 x 4096 | 9.5e-4 | 6.6e-3 |
| 12288 x 4096 | 9.4e-4 | 6.6e-3 |
| 4096 x 12288 | 1.5e-3 | 1.1e-2 |

The same shapes on gfx1201 with vLLM 0.27 gave 2.8e-4 at M = 64 and 512, so the large-M path differs between the two builds.

**Throughput**

Random 512 in / 256 out (token ids, so no chat tokens), same server settings:

| | c=1 tok/s (TPOT) | c=8 tok/s (TPOT) |
|---|---|---|

So on both RDNA3 and RDNA4 the speedup is there. The blocker for Qwen3 is the chat-template NaN described in my previous comment.
